summary: Practise temperature monitoring, excursion assessment, and corrective action for medicines and vaccines. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Pharmaceutical cold-chain quality training helps health supply-chain practitioners and quality officers investigate temperature events affecting medicines and vaccines. Participants practise reviewing logger records, reconstructing product exposure against label storage requirements, and documenting escalation and disposition decisions. They also map refrigeration and maintenance risks and develop corrective-action plans with traceable records for storage and distribution operations.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who manage, monitor, maintain, or quality-check the storage and distribution of temperature-sensitive medicines and vaccines.
modules: WHO EVM Records and Quality Controls
Cold Chain Reporting and Action Planning
prerequisites: No specific prior qualification is stated. Familiarity with health supply-chain, vaccine storage, medicine warehousing, refrigeration maintenance, or quality documentation will help you apply the exercises to your work. Coding is not required.
